title: Florida House, District 65
what_it_does: Represents District 65 (Part of Hillsborough) in the Florida House; votes on state laws and the state budget.
verified_ballot_note: Candidate list taken from the Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list on 2026-09-18 (https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp); statuses Qualified/Unopposed only. Counties from the Legislature's district listings.

candidates.name: Karen Gonzalez Pittman
candidates.occupation: State representative for District 65 since 2022; vice president of public affairs for Vein911 Vein Treatment Centers; former teacher
candidates.background: Third-generation Tampan and lifelong Hillsborough County resident with elementary education and measurement/evaluation degrees from USF. She taught for several years, worked in school evaluation offices and is vice president of public affairs for Vein911 and Health Performance Specialists. Married 25 years with four children.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

property_tax.summary: Voted yes on HJR 1-F in the June 2026 special session, which placed Amendment 3 on the November ballot to raise the homestead exemption for non-school property taxes to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028 and to limit how counties and cities may spend property-tax revenue.

sources.title: Florida House roll-call vote, CS/HJR 1F (Save our Homes from Excessive Property Taxes), passage 75-26

immigration.summary: Voted yes on SB 2-C (2025), which created the State Board of Immigration Enforcement, required state help with federal detainers, barred driver licenses for unauthorized immigrants, and funded an Unauthorized Alien Transport Program.

sources.title: Florida House roll-call vote, SB 2-C (Immigration), passage 85-30

abortion.summary: Voted no on SB 300 (2023), the law that limits most abortions after six weeks of pregnancy; the roll call does not record a stated reason.

sources.title: Florida House roll-call vote, SB 300 (Heartbeat Protection Act, six-week abortion limit), passage 70-40

guns.summary: Voted yes on HB 543 (2023), which allows carrying a concealed firearm without a state license.

sources.title: Florida House roll-call vote, CS/HB 543 (concealed carry without a license), passage 76-32

education_choice.summary: Voted yes on HB 1 (2023), which removed income limits and enrollment caps so state scholarship funds can follow any K-12 student to private or home education.

sources.title: Florida House roll-call vote, CS/CS/CS/CS/HB 1 (universal school-choice scholarships), passage 83-27

insurance.summary: Gonzalez Pittman said she would extend Florida's 1977 excess-profits law, which covers auto and commercial lines, to homeowners policies so homeowners get refunds when insurers make too much, and that refunds from utilities or local governments should be automatic.
insurance.quote: Expand a 1977 excess profits law that applies to car insurance and commercial insurance lines to homeowners policies.

sources.title: 2026 Florida election candidates: Midterm voter guide (Tampa Bay Times)

growth.summary: Gonzalez Pittman said stormwater needs to move faster and that Florida has to stop paving over quality of life before neighborhoods can handle new growth; she says she authored the state's new stormwater law.
growth.quote: ...we have to stop paving over our quality of life before our neighborhoods are ready to handle the new growth.

sources.title: 2026 Florida election candidates: Midterm voter guide (Tampa Bay Times)

environment.summary: Gonzalez Pittman said safeguarding power and water supplies should be one of two guiding principles on data centers, and that she would spend a $1 million appropriation accelerating a flood-reduction project.

sources.title: 2026 Florida election candidates: Midterm voter guide (Tampa Bay Times)

energy.summary: Gonzalez Pittman said refunds should be automatic when big utilities or local governments overcharge residents, and that she supported SB 484 so no Floridian is billed for power sent to a data center.

sources.title: 2026 Florida election candidates: Midterm voter guide (Tampa Bay Times)

healthcare.summary: Asked whether Medicaid should be cut or expanded, Gonzalez Pittman took neither side, saying she supports strong oversight of managed-care plans, timely payments to providers and increased transparency.

sources.title: 2026 Florida election candidates: Midterm voter guide (Tampa Bay Times)

candidates.name: Ben Braver
candidates.background: Science teacher who ran for state Senate District 23 in 2024 and is the Democratic nominee for HD 65 after the Aug. 18, 2026 primary.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

marijuana.summary: In an interview with Suncoast NORML, Braver pointed out that Florida voters approved medical marijuana in 2016 and that a majority backed adult-use legalization in 2024, and argued lawmakers have not responded to those results. He also called for evidence-based employment protections so medical cannabis patients are not fired over tests that do not measure impairment.

sources.title: Ben Braver Jumps in The Rotation - and Now He's Headed to the General Election

education_choice.summary: Braver, a public-school teacher, said Florida should address teacher shortages, pay and classroom resources and should reduce spending on the voucher program.

sources.title: Ben Braver Jumps in The Rotation - and Now He's Headed to the General Election

environment.summary: Braver, who teaches science, says protecting Florida's water supply, wetlands and natural resources from unsustainable development is a priority, and has spoken against energy-intensive data centers.

sources.title: Ben Braver Jumps in The Rotation - and Now He's Headed to the General Election

healthcare.summary: Braver said Medicaid needs to be expanded, which he said would cover about 800,000 more people with federal tax dollars Floridians have already paid.

sources.title: 2026 Florida election candidates: Midterm voter guide (Tampa Bay Times)

insurance.summary: Braver said bringing down insurance rates is a top priority and that the cost of living is high because monopolies control insurance, housing and energy; he would regulate companies with too much control and create a public option where competition does not exist.
insurance.quote: We can regulate companies that have too much control over you, ensure there is real competition and create a public option where there isn't.

sources.title: 2026 Florida election candidates: Midterm voter guide (Tampa Bay Times)

growth.summary: Braver said Florida should further regulate data centers, citing water use during the state's worst drought in 25 years, few permanent jobs, and public opposition.

sources.title: 2026 Florida election candidates: Midterm voter guide (Tampa Bay Times)

energy.summary: Braver said investing in solar energy is part of his plan to lower the cost of living.

sources.title: 2026 Florida election candidates: Midterm voter guide (Tampa Bay Times)

housing.summary: Braver said building truly affordable housing and mass transit is part of how he would lower living costs, and that money spent on data centers would do more good invested in affordable housing and schools.

sources.title: 2026 Florida election candidates: Midterm voter guide (Tampa Bay Times)

other_issues.title: Hope Florida
other_issues.summary: He confronted Gov. DeSantis over the Hope Florida settlement, accusing him of taking $10 million from a Medicaid settlement for political committees.

sources.title: Tampa Bay State Rep candidate confronts governor over Hope Florida scandal (Creative Loafing Tampa)

other_issues.title: Platform
other_issues.summary: NORML reports his priorities include affordable housing, functional schools, lower costs, clean water, government accountability and workers' rights.

sources.title: Ben Braver Jumps in The Rotation — and Now He's Headed to the General Election (Suncoast NORML)

other_issues.title: Workers' rights and government accountability
other_issues.summary: Braver says Florida lacks a state Department of Labor and ties cannabis employment protections to broader worker-protection gaps. He also argues corporate and donor influence in Tallahassee has pulled lawmakers away from what ordinary Floridians want.

sources.title: Ben Braver Jumps in The Rotation - and Now He's Headed to the General Election

other_issues.title: Housing and transit
other_issues.summary: A profile of his campaign describes him running on what it calls kitchen-table ideas aimed at monopolistic landlords and housing costs, and on addressing urban sprawl with public transit.

sources.title: Ben Braver's Bold Vision for Florida

other_issues.title: Teacher pay and money in politics
other_issues.summary: Braver named raising teacher wages his first priority, saying teachers must be able to afford to live in Florida, and getting big money out of politics his third. He said he would spend a $1 million appropriation on after-school programs in Hillsborough County schools.

sources.title: 2026 Florida election candidates: Midterm voter guide (Tampa Bay Times)
